notes.1: The majority of candidates correctly calculated the change in height of the oil level but then failed to convert the minutes into seconds.
notes.2: Candidates generally just multiplied the maximum speed of the vehicle by the time taken. However, they should have recognised that the car was accelerating and that the distance travelled was equal to the area under the graph ( maximum speed × time).
notes.3: Most candidates subtracted the starting speed from the final speed and divided by 2, rather than adding the speeds before dividing by 2.
notes.5: The vast majority of candidates thought that both the mass of the object and its weight increased when taken to the second planet.
notes.7: The majority of candidates thought that for the aircraft to travel at a constant speed, the driving force must be greater than the drag forces. Many also thought that for level flight the upward force must be greater than the weight of the aircraft.
notes.11: Candidates did not seem familiar with this activity. All options were selected and this indicated that many, including the better candidates, were unsure of the answer.
notes.12: Although a number of candidates correctly calculated the answer, an equal number simply multiplied the 400 by 0.02 not recognising that force is measured in newtons, not grams and that pressure is force divided by area.
notes.13: The majority of candidates thought that the distance from the bottom of the barometer tube, rather than the reservoir surface, to the mercury level in the tube was the required distance.
notes.14: Candidates were unsure of Brownian motion and there was evidence of guessing by most candidates with all options chosen.
notes.17: Few candidates showed an understanding of thermal capacity, with many thinking that the oil had the higher thermal capacity.
notes.22: Many candidates found this question challenging. Candidates would have benefited from observing wavefronts reflecting from barriers in order to gain an understanding of the behaviour of waves.
notes.24: Candidates had difficulty in understanding that the angle of refraction is the angle between the normal to the surface and the ray, rather than the angle between the surface and the ray and the majority of candidates therefore incorrectly gave option A as their answer.
notes.25: Few candidates were able to answer this question correctly.
notes.28: Candidates did not generally show an understanding of the properties of magnetically hard and magnetically soft metals.
notes.29: Only the strongest candidates answered correctly and worked out the poles induced on the ends of the magnets by the gap (both north-seeking poles) and then recognised that like poles repel each other.
notes.31: Stronger candidates were able to answer this question correctly and recognised that doubling the diameter quarters the resistance (not halving it as the resistance is inversely proportional to the cross sectional area) and that doubling the length doubles the resistance.
notes.33: Candidates struggled with this question with many being distracted by the LDR and thinking it must be the change in light level which would decrease the speed of the motor. However an increase in the light level would reduce the resistance of the LDR, increasing the current and increasing the speed of the motor.
notes.34: This was only answered correctly by the strongest candidates.
notes.35: Candidates were not aware that the fuse in a circuit should be connected in series with the appliance that is to be protected and in the live line. If a fuse in the neutral line blows then the potential difference between the live line and earth will remain high.
notes.37: The majority of candidates did not recognise that the two changes cancelled each other out. However stronger candidates recognised that swapping the poles reverses the direction of the force on the wire and changing the current direction also reverses the direction of the force, hence returning it to the original direction.
notes.40: This question proved challenging with all options chosen equally.
notes.key_messages:
Many candidates found this paper challenging and did not have the basic knowledge or understanding to
answer many of the questions. Nevertheless there were also some stronger candidates who showed some
understanding.
notes.general_comments:
Candidates answered Questions 4, 9, 16, 19, 21 and 27 well. However in general candidates found the test
challenging with Questions 1, 3, 5, 11, 13, 14, 17, 24, 25, 33 and 40 only answered correctly by the
strongest candidates.
